activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of Pan-Africanism
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concept of Pan-Africanism and its origins in the 15th Century
activities.learning_activity: (a) Examine the concept of Pan-Africanism (meaning, objectives and importance)
suggested_methods: Scenario: Guide students in manageable groups to recall and share their experiences of any of the school meeting they have attended in the past by focusing on the participants, objectives and importance of the meeting. Let them relate the findings with the meaning, participants, objectives and the importance of Pan-Africanism.
Debate: Divide students into two groups to debate on the relevance of Pan-Africanism in the current context.
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of Pan-Africanism is well examined
suggested_resources: Written texts and written text in braille on the concept of Pan-Africanism

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of Pan-Africanism
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concept of Pan-Africanism and its origins in the 15th Century
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain the origins of Pan- Africanism in the 15th Century (Trans- Atlantic Slave Trade and people of African origin in the New World)
suggested_methods: Think-Ink- Pair- Share: Task students in each group to think of and present a short report on factors that contribute to family/ society unity and good relationships. Let them relate their responses with the origins of Pan-Africanism in the 15th Century.
activities.assessment_criteria: The origin of Pan-Africanism in the 15th Century is well explained
suggested_resources: Written texts and written text in braille on origin of Pan-Africanism
Maps and photos on Trans- Atlantic Slave Trade

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of Pan-Africanism
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of the development of Pan-Africanism from the 16th to 19th Century
activities.learning_activity: Discuss the development of Pan- Africanism from the 16th to 19th Century (slavery and colonial systems in the New World, Back to Africa Movement and Black Solidarity)
suggested_methods: Library research/ resource room: Assign students in groups to read from relevant references/sources on the development of Pan- Africanism during the slavery and colonial systems from the 16th to the 19th Century. Let them discuss and share the findings in the whole class.
activities.assessment_criteria: The development of Pan-Africanism from 16th to 19th Century is clearly discussed
suggested_resources: Online resources on the development of Pan-Africanism from 16th to 19th Century

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of Pan-Africanism
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of Pan-Africanism during colonial time and during the struggle against colonialism from 1900 to 1960

suggested_methods: Discussion: Assign students in groups to read relevant references on the development of Pan- Africanism during the first half of the 20th Century and share the findings in the whole class.
activities.assessment_criteria: The development of Pan-Africanism during the first half of the 20th Century is well examined
suggested_resources: Written texts and written text in Braille on Pan-Africanism

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of Pan-Africanism
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of Pan-Africanism during colonial time and during the struggle against colonialism from 1900 to 1960
activities.learning_activity: (b) Discuss the contribution of Pan-Africanism to anti-colonial struggles in Africa (conferences and their resolutions)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Divide students into manageable groups to explore the contributions of Pan-Africanism (focus on conferences and their resolutions) on the African struggles against colonialism and share the findings in the whole class.
activities.assessment_criteria: The contribution of Pan-Africanism to anti-colonial struggles in Africa is well assessed
suggested_resources: Written text, and written texts in braille on Pan-Africanism and Ant-colonial struggles

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of Pan-Africanism
activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of Pan-Africanism since 1960
activities.learning_activity: Analyse the development of Pan-Africanism since 1960s (African unity, struggles against neo-colonialism, Apartheid and globalization)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Divide students into manageable groups to explore the development of Pan-Africanism since 1960 (focus on African unity, struggles against neo-colonialism, Apartheid, and globalization), and share the findings in the whole class for discussion.
activities.assessment_criteria: The development of Pan-Africanism since 1960 is well analysed

activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industrialisation in different nations during the 18th and 19th Centuries
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the concept of industrial revolution (meaning, processes and characteristics)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students in manageable groups to read relevant references on the meaning, process and characteristics of industrial revolution in the 18th and 19th Centuries and share the findings in the whole class. Let them summarise for reference.
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of industrial revolution is well explained

Pictures/ photos of industries

activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industrialisation in different nations during the 18th and 19th Centuries
activities.learning_activity: (b) Compare the Industrial Revolution of Britain with the revolutions in Belgium, France, Germany, USA and Japan
suggested_methods: Jigsaw: Divide students into manageable groups and assign each group a country (Belgium, France, Germany, USA, and Japan) to study country’s industrial revolution and compare it with that of Britain. Let each group share the findings in the whole class for discussions.
activities.assessment_criteria: The industrial revolutions of Britain and Belgium, France, Germany, USA and Japan are well compared
suggested_resources: Written documents and written texts in braille on industries

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of the industrial revolution
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industrialisation in different nations during the 18th and 19th Centuries
activities.learning_activity: (c) Discuss the impacts of the 18th and 19th Centuries industrial revolutions on the world
suggested_methods: Scenario: Let each student to imagine some farmers in a village have started to mechanise their farming activities instead of manual work. Ask them to share in the whole class what will be the expected results and impacts on the farmers and the villagers. Let them relate their imaginations and the impacts of the 18th and 19th Centuries industrial revolutions, then allow class discussions.
activities.assessment_criteria: The impacts of industrial revolution of the 18th and 19th Centuries are well discussed
suggested_resources: Written texts and written texts in braille on Industrial revolution

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of the industrial revolution
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industralisation in different nations from the 20th Century to the present

suggested_methods: Library research/ resource room: Assign students in groups to read from relevant references/sources on the rise of the industrial revolution of the 20th Century (Asia and Latin America) and their impacts on the world. Allow the students to share the findings in the whole class for discussions and summary.
activities.assessment_criteria: The industrial revolutions of the 20th Century and their impacts are well discussed
suggested_resources: Written texts and written texts in braille on Industrial revolution of the 20th Century
Pictures/ photos of industries

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of the industrial revolution
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industralisation in different nations from the 20th Century to the present
activities.learning_activity: (b) Discuss the changes and continuities between the industrial revolutions of the 18th and 19th Centuries and those of the 20th Century
suggested_methods: Discussion: Divide students into manageable groups to explore changes and continuities of the 18th and 19th Centuries and those of the 20th Century. Let the groups share their explorations in the whole class for discussions
activities.assessment_criteria: The changes and continuities between industrial revolution of the 18th and 19th Centuries and those of the 20th Century are well examined
suggested_resources: Written texts and written text in braille on changes of industrial revolution of 18th and 19th Centuries

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of the industrial revolution
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industralisation in different nations from the 20th Century to the present
activities.learning_activity: (c) Discuss the nature and character of the Fourth Industrial Revolution evolving in the 21st Century
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students in manageable groups to explore the nature and character of the Fourth industrial revolution developing in the 21st Century
activities.assessment_criteria: The nature and character of the Fourth industrial revolution is well examined
suggested_resources: Written texts and written texts in braille on the fourth industrial revolution

activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industralisation in different nations from the 20th Century to the present
activities.learning_activity: (d) Discuss the impacts of the Fourth industrial revolution on global changes in socio-economic and political patterns (digital technology, smart economy, e- government, e-commerce) development patterns
suggested_methods: ICT support learning: Divide students into manageable groups and assign them with appropriate references from the internet such as journal articles, and books to study on the impact of the Fourth industrial revolution on global changes by emphasising on socio-economic and political patterns (digital technology, smart economy. Let each group share the findings in the whole class for discussions.
activities.assessment_criteria: The impacts of the fourth industrial revolution on global changes in socio-economic and political patterns are clearly examined

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of the industrial revolution
activities.specific_competence: 2.3 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industralisation in Africa
activities.learning_activity: (a) Discuss the nature and character of industrial development in Africa from the 1960s to the present
suggested_methods: Project: Divide the students into manageable groups and assign each group a country to examine the nature and character of industrial development from the 1960s to the present. Let them write a report, present to the whole class for discussion before submission.
activities.assessment_criteria: The nature and character of industrial development in Africa from the 1960s to the present is well assessed
suggested_resources: Written texts and sketch maps the nature and character of industrial development in Africa from the 1960s to the present

activities.specific_competence: 2.3 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of industralisation in Africa
activities.learning_activity: (b) Examine lessons learnt from the industrial revolutions of the 19th, 20th and 21st Centuries which can be applied to bring about industrial development in Africa
suggested_methods: Self-Reflection: In manageable groups let students to reflect on, and write about lessons that African countries can learn to develop their industries from the 19th, 20th and 21st Centuries` industrial development. Let students present the responses to all members of the class.
activities.assessment_criteria: The lessons learnt from the industrial revolutions of the 19th, 20th and 21th Centuries to bring industrial development in Africa are clearly examined
suggested_resources: Online resource and wall maps on industrial revolution of the 19th, 20th and 21st Centuries

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of administrative systems in the world
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the origins of administrative systems in the ancient world

Guide them to relate and discuss their responses on the concepts of administration and administrative systems (emphasise on meaning, types and advantages and disadvantages)
activities.assessment_criteria: The concepts of administration and administrative systems are well examined

suggested_methods: Jigsaw: Divide students into five groups and assign each group to explore indigenous concepts and practices of administrative systems in either pre- colonial Africa or Ancient Europe or South America or Asia or the Middle East. Let each group share the findings in the whole class for discussion and summary.
activities.assessment_criteria: The indigenous concepts and practices of administration and administrative systems in different global contexts are well examined

activities.learning_activity: (b) Discuss the extent to which religious principles led to changes in administrative systems in the world from the Middle Ages to the 18th Century (indigenous religions in different global contexts, Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Confucianism, Shintoism Judaism, and African religions)

Let each group focus on either Christianity or, Islam, Buddhism or Confucianism or Shintoism or Judaism, or African religion. Let each group present the findings in a class for discussion.

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of threats to world peace

activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of threats to world peace and security is clearly explained

Let each group focus on either the Westphalia Treaty or sovereignty or balance of power or military alliances. Let each group present the findings in a class for discussion.
activities.assessment_criteria: The ways in which great wars fought from the 17th to the 19th Century generated new ideas on world peace and security are clearly discussed

activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of the threats to world peace resulting from civil and ethnic wars
activities.learning_activity: Examine the nature and character of ethnic and civil wars and the threats they pose on world peace and security ( Kosovo conflict, Rwanda and Burundi Civil Wars, Somalia, Central Africa Republic, Mali, Rohingya, Cambodia, Yemen, the Palestinian-Israel conflict)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students in their groups to explore from references the meaning of ethnic and civil war. Let them investigate the nature and character of each ethnic and civil wars and the threats they pose on world peace and security by focusing on Kosovo conflict, Rwanda and Burundi Civil Wars, Somalia, Rohingya, Cambodia, Yemen, and the Palestinian-Israel conflict. Let groups share the findings of each group to the whole class for discuss
activities.assessment_criteria: The nature and character of ethnic and civil wars and threats to world peace and security is clearly examined
suggested_resources: ICT devices with contents on ethnic and inter-ethnic wars

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of threats to world peace
activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of the threats to world peace resulting from civil and ethnic wars
activities.learning_activity: Examine the extent to which ethnic and civil wars are connected to the global industrial-military complex
suggested_methods: Case study: Let students in groups study a case of the USA, Britain, France, Russia, China and Germany industrial military complex. From the case study, allow students to investigate the extent to which ethnic and civil wars are connected with the global industrial-military complex.
activities.assessment_criteria: The connection between ethnic and civil wars to global industrial military complex is well examined
suggested_resources: Online resources on the relationship between ethnic wars and global industrial military complex

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of threats to world peace
activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of the threats to world peace resulting from civil and ethnic wars
activities.learning_activity: Discuss peace building strategies in countries affected by ethnic and civil wars
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss how their societies build and maintain peace and share their ideas with the whole class. Let students in groups to relate their findings with the peace building strategies in countries affected by ethnic and civil wars.
activities.assessment_criteria: The peace building strategies are well discussed
suggested_resources: Online resources on peace building strategies

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of development in Africa
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of development in post-colonial Africa
activities.learning_activity: Explain the concept of development in post-colonial Africa (meaning and indicators)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students in groups to brainstorm on the concept of development and let them identify different indicators of development in post-colonial Africa. Facilitate them to present in the class for discussion.
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of development in post-colonial Africa is well explained
suggested_resources: Online resources on the concept of development in post-colonial Africa

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of development in Africa
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of development in post-colonial Africa
activities.learning_activity: Appraise political, economic, and social developments in different regions of Africa from the 1960 to present ( Eastern, Western, Southern and Northern Africa)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students in groups to investigate on political, economic, and social developments that are available in their society and share in the class, and then let them evaluate and share the political, economic, and social developments in different countries in Africa from Eastern, Western, Southern and Northern African regions from the 1960 to the present.
activities.assessment_criteria: Political, economic and social developments in different regions of Africa from the 1960s to present are well evaluated
suggested_resources: ICT devices with contents political, economic, and social developments in different regions of Africa from the 1960 to present

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the history of development in Africa
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the history of development in post-colonial Africa
activities.learning_activity: Discuss the internal and external factors hindering political, social, technological and economic development in Africa from the 1960s to the present
suggested_methods: Think-Ink-Pair- Share: Guide students in groups to identify the factors hindering development in their societies and share their ideas in the class.
Discussion: Facilitate students to discuss and share the internal and external factors hindering political, social, technological, and economic developments in Africa from the 1960s to the present
activities.assessment_criteria: The internal and external factors hindering political, social, technological, and economic development in Africa from the 1960s to the present are well discussed.
suggested_resources: Online resources on internal and external factors hindering political, social, technological and economic development in Africa from the 1960s to the present

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Conduct a project in History
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Conduct a project in History
activities.learning_activity: Complete and submit for assessment the project initiated in Form Five
suggested_methods: Guide the students to write and submit a report on the project initiated in Form Five
activities.assessment_criteria: A project in History is well written and submitted for assessment
suggested_resources: Online resources conducting project in History
